pool: Which verse from today could you pray again before you sleep?
Where did you find yourself today: in the lament, the trust, or the praise?
Which line would you like to learn by heart?
Whom could you pray today's psalms for?
What did today's psalms ask you to let go of?
When did you last thank God the way the psalmist does?
Which psalm today sounded most like your own prayer?
Which name of God stood out to you today?

days.intro: The Psalter opens with the two ways, the blessed man and the ungodly, and with the Lord and His Christ. Watch how quickly these psalms move from distress to trust, and end in wonder at God's name in all the earth.
days.q: Psalm 1 sets two ways before us. What helps you keep to the way of the blessed man?

days.intro: These psalms carry the cry 'How long, O Lord?' beside a firm trust. Psalm 15 is the psalm the Apostle Peter read of the Resurrection: 'thou wilt not leave my soul in hell' (Acts 2).
days.q: Psalm 14 asks who shall dwell in the Lord's tabernacle. Which of its answers do you most need to grow in?

days.intro: From 'I will love thee, O Lord, my strength' to 'Who is this King of glory?'. Psalm 21 begins with the words Christ cried on the Cross, and Psalm 22 is 'The Lord tends me as a shepherd' (23 in most Bibles).
days.q: Christ prayed Psalm 21 on the Cross. What does it mean to you that He prayed a psalm there?

days.intro: Light and trust run through these psalms: 'The Lord is my light and my Saviour; whom shall I fear?' Psalm 30 holds the words Christ spoke as He gave up His spirit: 'Into thine hands I will commit my spirit.'
days.q: Psalm 26 asks, 'Whom shall I fear?' What fear would you hand over to the Lord today?

days.intro: 'Taste and see that the Lord is good' (Psalm 33) is sung as Communion is given at the Presanctified Liturgy, and 'in thy light we shall see light' (Psalm 35) is sung in the Great Doxology at Matins.
days.q: Psalm 36 says, 'Fret not thyself because of evil-doers.' What do you need to stop fretting over?

days.intro: Psalm 37 is one of the six psalms read at the start of Matins, a prayer of repentance. Psalm 41 is the thirst of the deer for the fountains of water, and Psalm 44 the Church sings of the Mother of God.
days.q: Psalm 41 speaks of a soul that longs for God as a deer for water. When have you felt that thirst?

days.intro: At the centre of this kathisma stands Psalm 50, 'Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy great mercy', David's psalm of repentance, which the Church prays every day.
days.q: Psalm 50 asks for a clean heart. What would you ask God to make new in you?

days.intro: Psalm 62, 'O God, my God, I cry to thee early', is another of the six psalms of Matins. Here David prays in hiding and in danger, and keeps coming back to trust: 'I have hoped in God; I will not be afraid.'
days.q: Psalm 62 seeks God early. What would change if you gave Him the first minutes of your day?

days.intro: Psalm 67 begins 'Let God arise, and let his enemies be scattered', the verse the Church sings again and again at Pascha. Psalm 68 foretells the vinegar given to Christ on the Cross.
days.q: 'Let God arise' is a Paschal cry. Where do you most need to see Christ's victory today?

days.intro: Psalm 71 sees a King who 'shall come down as rain upon a fleece', which the Church sings of the Word taking flesh of the Virgin. Psalm 72 is honest about envying the proud, until the psalmist goes into the sanctuary of God.
days.q: Psalm 72 nearly envies the proud until it enters God's house. What helps you see things truly again?

days.intro: Psalm 77 retells Israel's story and the bread from heaven, which Christ took up when He called Himself the Bread of Life (John 6). Psalm 81's 'Arise, O God, judge the earth' is sung on Holy Saturday.
days.q: Psalm 83 says one day in God's courts is better than thousands. What does a day near God look like for you?

days.intro: Here are Psalm 87, the darkest of the six psalms of Matins, and Psalm 90, 'He that dwells in the help of the Highest', prayed at the Sixth Hour for God's protection.
days.q: Psalm 89 asks God to teach us to number our days. How would you like to spend the days you are given?

days.intro: A kathisma of praise. 'The Lord reigns; he has clothed himself with honour' (Psalm 92) is sung at Vespers on Saturday evening, as the Lord's day begins. Psalm 94 warns, 'harden not your hearts.'
days.q: Psalm 94 says, 'To-day, if ye will hear his voice.' What might the Lord be asking of you today?

days.intro: Psalm 102, 'Bless the Lord, O my soul', is sung at the beginning of the Divine Liturgy in many churches, and Psalm 103, the hymn of creation, opens Vespers. Psalm 104 remembers God's faithfulness from Abraham to the Exodus.
days.q: Psalm 102 says, 'forget not all his praises.' What gift of God have you forgotten to thank Him for?

days.intro: These psalms confess Israel's long unfaithfulness and God's longer mercy. In Psalm 106 travellers, prisoners, the sick and sailors all cry to the Lord in their trouble, and He brings them out.
days.q: In Psalm 106 everyone in trouble cries to the Lord and is heard. What trouble would you bring to Him now?

days.intro: Psalm 109, 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand', is the verse Christ Himself put to the Pharisees. Psalm 117 gives 'Blessed is he that comes in the name of the Lord' and 'This is the day which the Lord has made.'
days.q: Psalm 115 asks, 'What shall I render to the Lord for all the things wherein he has rewarded me?' What is your answer today?

days.intro: One psalm, the longest: Psalm 118, twenty-two stanzas, every verse turning on God's word and law. The Church reads it at the Midnight Office and at the burial of the dead. Read it slowly; it is meant to be prayed, not hurried.
days.q: Which verse of Psalm 118 would you like to carry with you this week?

days.intro: The Songs of Ascents, sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem: 'I was glad when they said to me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.' Psalm 127 is sung at the Orthodox wedding, and Psalm 129, 'Out of the depths', at Vespers.
days.q: Psalm 126 says, 'Except the Lord build the house, they that build labour in vain.' What are you building without asking Him?

days.intro: Psalms 134 and 135, 'for his mercy endures for ever', are sung at festal Matins; Psalm 136, 'By the rivers of Babylon', on the Sundays before Lent; and Psalm 140, 'Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense', at every Vespers.
days.q: Psalm 138 says there is nowhere we can go from God's presence. What is it like to be known that fully?

days.intro: The Psalter ends in praise. Psalm 144 gives the prayer before meals, 'The eyes of all wait upon thee', and Psalms 148 to 150, 'Let every thing that has breath praise the Lord', are sung at Matins.
days.q: As you finish the Psalter, what will you praise God for?

pool: Which word of Christ from today would you like to remember tomorrow?
Where do you see yourself in today's chapter?
What does today's chapter show you about who Christ is?
Whom could you pray for after reading today's chapter?
What did today's chapter ask you to change?
Which person in today's chapter would you like to be more like?
What would you like to ask Christ about today's chapter?
How could you live one line of today's chapter before the day ends?

days.intro: Matthew opens with the generations from Abraham to Christ, then the angel's word to Joseph. Watch for the name given before He is born: Emmanuel, 'God with us.'
days.q: Joseph did what the angel told him without a word recorded. Where is God asking for your quiet obedience?

days.intro: The wise men come from the East to worship the Child, while Herod seeks to destroy Him. Watch the difference between those who seek Christ to worship and those who seek Him to do harm.
days.q: The wise men brought gold, frankincense and myrrh. What gift could you bring to Christ this week?

days.intro: John the Baptist calls Israel to repentance, and Christ comes to be baptized. At the Jordan the Holy Trinity is made known: the Father's voice, the Son in the water, the Spirit descending like a dove.
days.q: John says, 'Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance.' What would that fruit look like in your life?

days.intro: Christ fasts forty days and answers each temptation with the word of Scripture. Then He calls the first disciples from their nets: 'Follow me.'
days.q: Peter and Andrew left their nets at once. What would be hardest for you to leave to follow Him?

days.intro: The Sermon on the Mount begins. Watch for whom Christ calls blessed, and how He fulfils the Law rather than setting it aside.
days.q: Which of the Beatitudes asks the most of you this week?

days.intro: Christ teaches almsgiving, prayer and fasting done in secret, and gives the Lord's Prayer. He ends by asking us to seek first the kingdom of God and not to be anxious about tomorrow.
days.q: Which line of the Lord's Prayer is hardest for you to pray honestly?

days.intro: The Sermon ends: judge not, ask and it shall be given you, enter in at the strait gate. Watch the closing picture of two houses, one built on rock and one on sand.
days.q: Christ speaks of the beam in our own eye. Whom have you been quick to judge?

days.intro: Come down from the mountain, Christ heals a leper, a centurion's servant and Peter's wife's mother, and calms the storm. Watch the centurion's faith, greater than Christ had found in Israel.
days.q: In the storm the disciples cried, 'Lord, save us.' What storm would you ask Him to calm?

days.intro: Christ forgives a paralysed man his sins, calls Matthew from the receipt of custom, and eats with sinners: 'I will have mercy, and not sacrifice.' A woman touches the hem of His garment and is healed.
days.q: Matthew rose and followed Him. With whom does Christ want you to share your table?

days.intro: Christ names the twelve Apostles and sends them out. He warns of persecution and promises that not one sparrow falls to the ground without the Father.
days.q: Christ says the very hairs of your head are numbered. Where do you need to trust that care today?

days.intro: From prison John asks whether Jesus is He that should come. Christ answers with His works, and ends with an invitation: 'Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden.'
days.q: What burden would you bring to Christ in exchange for His easy yoke?

days.intro: Disputes over the sabbath grow sharp, yet Christ heals and will not break a bruised reed. He speaks of the sign of Jonah, and calls those who do the Father's will His brother, sister and mother.
days.q: 'Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.' What have your words shown about your heart lately?

days.intro: A chapter of parables: the sower, the wheat and the tares, the mustard seed, the treasure and the pearl. Watch what each one says about how the kingdom grows: hidden, small, and worth everything.
days.q: In the parable of the sower, which kind of ground is your heart today?

days.intro: John the Baptist is beheaded. Christ feeds five thousand with five loaves, then comes to the disciples walking on the sea, and catches Peter when he begins to sink.
days.q: Peter began to sink when he saw the wind. What makes you take your eyes off Christ?

days.intro: Christ teaches that what defiles comes out of the heart, not what goes into the mouth. A woman of Canaan will not stop asking, and He praises her great faith.
days.q: The woman of Canaan kept asking, humbly. What have you stopped asking God for?

days.intro: At Caesarea Philippi Peter confesses, 'Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.' Then Christ speaks for the first time of His Passion, and calls His followers to take up their cross.
days.q: Christ asks, 'Whom say ye that I am?' How would you answer Him today, in your own words?

days.intro: On the mountain Christ is transfigured before Peter, James and John, His face shining as the sun. The Father's voice says, 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.'
days.q: Coming down from the mountain they met a suffering boy. How does prayer send you back to people in need?

days.intro: Christ sets a child in the midst of the disciples and speaks of humility, the lost sheep, and forgiveness. Peter asks how often to forgive, and hears 'seventy times seven' and the parable of the unforgiving servant.
days.q: The parable ends with forgiving 'from your hearts'. Whom do you need to forgive that way?

days.intro: Christ speaks of marriage, blesses the little children, and meets a rich young man who goes away sorrowful. 'With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.'
days.q: The young man went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions. What possession holds you back?

days.intro: Labourers hired at the eleventh hour receive the same wage as the first, a parable St John Chrysostom's Paschal homily takes up. Christ teaches that whoever will be great must be the servant of all.
days.q: Christ came 'not to be ministered unto, but to minister'. Whom could you serve quietly this week?

days.intro: Christ enters Jerusalem, meek and sitting upon an ass, as the crowds cry 'Hosanna': the feast of Palm Sunday. He cleanses the temple and tells the parable of the vineyard's wicked husbandmen.
days.q: In the parable of the two sons, one said no and then went. Where do your words and your deeds not yet agree?

days.intro: The parable of the wedding feast, the tribute money, and the question of the resurrection. Asked for the great commandment, Christ answers: love God with all your heart, and your neighbour as yourself.
days.q: What does it mean for you to love God 'with all thy mind'?

days.intro: Christ speaks woes against hypocrisy, a faith kept only on the outside. It ends with His lament over Jerusalem: 'how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens.'
days.q: Christ warns against cleaning only the outside of the cup. What in you needs cleaning on the inside?

days.intro: On the mount of Olives Christ foretells the fall of the temple and the signs of the end. Watch for His word again and again: be ready, for of that day and hour knoweth no man.
days.q: If the Lord came today, what would you want to have set right?

days.intro: The ten virgins, the talents, and the Last Judgment, read on the Sunday of the Last Judgment before Lent: 'Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.'
days.q: Who are 'the least of these' you meet in your own week?

days.intro: The Passion begins: the anointing at Bethany, the Mystical Supper where Christ gives His Body and Blood, the prayer in Gethsemane, the betrayal, and Peter's denial. Read it slowly, as the Church does in Holy Week.
days.q: In Gethsemane Christ prayed, 'not as I will, but as thou wilt.' Where do you need to pray those words?

days.intro: Christ is delivered to Pilate, mocked, crucified, and laid in the tomb. Watch who stays: the women beholding afar off, Joseph of Arimathaea, and the centurion who says, 'Truly this was the Son of God.'
days.q: Simon of Cyrene was made to bear the Cross. Whose cross could you help to carry?

days.intro: Christ is risen. The women meet Him and hold Him by the feet, and on a mountain in Galilee He sends the Eleven to all nations, baptizing in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost.
days.q: Christ ends with 'lo, I am with you alway.' Where do you most need to remember that today?

days.intro: Mark begins at speed: John in the wilderness, the Baptism, the temptation, and Christ's first words, 'The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.'
days.q: Christ rose a great while before day to pray alone. When could you find a quiet time to pray?

days.intro: Four friends let a paralysed man down through a roof, and Christ first forgives his sins. He calls Levi and teaches that the sabbath was made for man.
days.q: The paralysed man was carried by four friends. Whom could you carry to Christ in prayer?

days.intro: Christ heals a withered hand on the sabbath, ordains the Twelve 'that they should be with him', and answers those who say He casts out devils by Beelzebub.
days.q: The Twelve were chosen first 'to be with him'. How much of your day is simply time with Christ?

days.intro: The parable of the sower, the seed that springs and grows while the sower sleeps, and the mustard seed. In the evening Christ stills the storm: 'Peace, be still.'
days.q: The seed grows 'he knoweth not how'. Where do you need patience with God's slow work in you?

days.intro: Christ frees a man possessed by a legion of devils, heals a woman who touches His garment in faith, and raises Jairus' daughter: 'Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.'
days.q: The healed man wanted to follow Christ but was told, 'Go home to thy friends.' Where is your own place to bear witness?

days.intro: In Nazareth Christ marvels at their unbelief. He sends out the Twelve, John the Baptist is put to death, and five thousand are fed in a desert place.
days.q: Christ said, 'Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while.' What would real rest with Him look like for you?

days.intro: Christ warns against holding the tradition of men while laying aside the commandment of God. He heals a deaf man with one word, 'Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.'
days.q: If Christ said 'Be opened' to you, what would you ask Him to open?

days.intro: A blind man is healed in two touches, first seeing 'men as trees, walking'. Then Peter confesses Christ, and Christ teaches that whoever loses his life for His sake and the gospel's shall save it.
days.q: Like the blind man, do you see clearly yet, or only in part? What would you ask Him to show you?

days.intro: After the Transfiguration a father cries out, 'Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief', a Gospel the Church reads in Great Lent. Christ teaches that the first must be servant of all.
days.q: 'Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.' Where do belief and doubt sit side by side in you?

days.intro: Christ blesses the children, looks with love on the rich young man, and says He came 'to give his life a ransom for many'. Blind Bartimaeus cries out, is healed, and follows Him in the way.
days.q: Christ asked Bartimaeus, 'What wilt thou that I should do unto thee?' What is your answer?

days.intro: Christ enters Jerusalem to cries of 'Hosanna', cleanses the temple, which is to be a house of prayer for all nations, and teaches that prayer needs both faith and forgiveness.
days.q: Christ says, 'when ye stand praying, forgive.' Whom do you need to forgive before you pray?

days.intro: Questions about tribute, the resurrection and the first commandment. The chapter ends with a poor widow who casts in two mites, all that she had.
days.q: The widow gave of her want. What could you give that would truly cost you something?

days.intro: Christ foretells the fall of the temple and the trials to come, and ends with one word for everyone: 'Watch.'
days.q: What does it look like for you to watch, in an ordinary week?

days.intro: A woman pours precious ointment on Christ's head, and He says, 'She hath done what she could.' Then the Supper, the agony in Gethsemane, 'Abba, Father', the arrest, and Peter's denial.
days.q: Christ said of the woman, 'She hath done what she could.' What could you do for Him today?

days.intro: Christ before Pilate, the crown of thorns, the Cross, the cry 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?', and His burial. Mark names the women who looked on to the end.
days.q: The women stayed near the Cross when others fled. What helps you stay near Christ when it is hard?

days.intro: The myrrh-bearing women find the stone rolled away and hear, 'He is risen; he is not here.' Christ appears to Mary Magdalene, sends the Eleven into all the world, and is received up into heaven.
days.q: The women were the first to hear that Christ is risen. Who first told you?

days.intro: The angel Gabriel comes to Zacharias in the temple and to the Virgin Mary in Nazareth. Watch Mary's answer, 'be it unto me according to thy word', and her song, 'My soul doth magnify the Lord', sung at Matins.
days.q: Mary said, 'be it unto me according to thy word.' What is hardest for you to say yes to?

days.intro: Christ is born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger, and the angels sing, 'Glory to God in the highest.' In the temple Simeon takes Him in his arms and says the prayer the Church sings at Vespers: 'Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace.'
days.q: Simeon waited all his life to see the Lord. What are you waiting on God for?

days.intro: John tells the people what repentance means in practice: share your coat, take no more than is due. Then the Baptism, and the generations of Christ traced back to Adam, 'which was the son of God'.
days.q: The people asked John, 'What shall we do then?' What would he tell you?

days.intro: After the temptation Christ reads Isaiah in the synagogue at Nazareth: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor.'
days.q: Christ came to heal the brokenhearted. What broken place in you would you bring to Him?

days.intro: At Christ's word Peter lets down the net and it breaks with fish. Peter falls down: 'Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.' Christ answers, 'Fear not.'
days.q: Peter toiled all night and took nothing until Christ spoke. Where have you been working without asking Him?

days.intro: Christ continues all night in prayer, then chooses the Twelve. On the plain He says, 'Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you', and 'Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.'
days.q: Who is hard for you to love right now? What is one good thing you could do for them?

days.intro: Christ raises the only son of a widow at Nain, moved with compassion. At Simon's table a woman who was a sinner washes His feet with her tears, and He forgives her, 'for she loved much'.
days.q: She loved much because she was forgiven much. What has God forgiven you that you could thank Him for?

days.intro: Women follow Christ and minister to Him of their substance. He tells the parable of the sower, stills the storm, and raises Jairus' daughter.
days.q: Christ asked who had touched Him. If He asked you why you came to Him, what would you say?

days.intro: Christ feeds the five thousand, Peter confesses Him, and the Transfiguration follows. Then Christ 'stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem'.
days.q: Christ asks us to take up our cross daily. What is your cross today?

days.intro: Christ sends out the Seventy, tells the parable of the Good Samaritan, and visits Martha and Mary: 'one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part.'
days.q: The Samaritan saw the wounded man and had compassion on him. Whom have you passed by on the other side?

days.intro: A disciple asks, 'Lord, teach us to pray', and Christ gives the Lord's Prayer and the parable of the friend at midnight: ask, seek, knock.
days.q: The friend kept knocking at midnight. What have you been praying for that you are tempted to give up on?

days.intro: Christ tells of a rich man who built greater barns and died that night: 'So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.' Consider the ravens, consider the lilies.
days.q: What would it mean for you to be rich toward God?

days.intro: Christ calls everyone to repentance and tells of a barren fig tree given one more year. On the sabbath He heals a woman bowed together for eighteen years.
days.q: The fig tree was given one more year. What fruit would you like your life to bear this year?

days.intro: At a dinner Christ teaches to sit down in the lowest room, and to call the poor, who cannot recompense you. Then the parable of the great supper and the cost of following Him.
days.q: Christ says to invite those who cannot repay you. Whom could you welcome this week?

days.intro: Three parables of the lost: the sheep, the piece of silver, and the son who comes home, read on the Sunday of the Prodigal Son before Lent. Watch the father, who sees his son a great way off and runs.
days.q: The prodigal son 'came to himself'. What would coming to yourself look like?

days.intro: The parable of the unjust steward and the saying, 'Ye cannot serve God and mammon.' Then the rich man and Lazarus, who was laid at his gate.
days.q: Lazarus was laid at the rich man's gate every day. Who is at your gate?

days.intro: Ten lepers are cleansed, and only one, a Samaritan, turns back to give thanks. Christ also says, 'the kingdom of God is within you.'
days.q: Only one of the ten came back to give thanks. What have you forgotten to thank God for?

days.intro: Two parables of prayer: the widow who would not give up, and the Pharisee and the publican, read on the first Sunday of the Triodion. 'God be merciful to me a sinner.'
days.q: The publican prayed in a few words. What would your own short prayer of the heart be?

days.intro: Zacchaeus climbs a sycomore tree to see Christ, and Christ says, 'to day I must abide at thy house.' Then the entry into Jerusalem, and Christ weeps over the city.
days.q: Zacchaeus changed the day Christ came to his house. What would change if Christ came to yours today?

days.intro: In the temple Christ is questioned about His authority, about tribute to Caesar, and about the resurrection. He answers that God 'is not a God of the dead, but of the living: for all live unto him.'
days.q: 'All live unto him.' Whom among the departed would you remember in prayer today?

days.intro: A poor widow casts in two mites, all she had. Christ foretells the trials to come and says, 'In your patience possess ye your souls.'
days.q: Christ asks for patience in trial. Where do you most need patience right now?

days.intro: At the Supper Christ gives His Body and Blood: 'this do in remembrance of me.' On the mount of Olives He prays in agony. After Peter's denial 'the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter', and Peter wept bitterly.
days.q: The Lord looked at Peter after the denial, and Peter wept. What would that look stir in you?

days.intro: From the Cross Christ prays, 'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do', and promises the thief, 'To day shalt thou be with me in paradise'. The Church takes up the thief's words before Communion: 'Remember me, O Lord, in Thy Kingdom.'
days.q: The thief asked only to be remembered. What would you ask Christ to remember of you?

days.intro: 'Why seek ye the living among the dead?' On the road to Emmaus Christ walks with two disciples, opens the Scriptures to them, and is known of them in breaking of bread.
days.q: Their hearts burned as He opened the Scriptures. When has a passage burned in your heart?

days.intro: 'In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.' John's prologue is read at the Paschal Liturgy. Then John the Baptist points to Christ: 'Behold the Lamb of God.'
days.q: Philip told Nathanael, 'Come and see.' Whom could you invite to come and see?

days.intro: At a marriage in Cana, at His Mother's word, Christ turns water into wine, the beginning of His signs. Her words to the servants are for us too: 'Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.'
days.q: The Mother of God said, 'Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.' What has He been saying to you?

days.intro: Nicodemus comes to Christ by night and hears of being born 'of water and of the Spirit', and of the Father's love: 'For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son.'
days.q: John the Baptist said, 'He must increase, but I must decrease.' Where could you step aside so that Christ is seen?

days.intro: At Jacob's well Christ asks a woman of Samaria for a drink and offers her living water. She leaves her waterpot and tells her whole city. The Church remembers her as St Photini.
days.q: The woman left her waterpot to tell others. What would you leave behind to share what Christ has done for you?

days.intro: At the pool of Bethesda a man has waited thirty-eight years. Christ asks, 'Wilt thou be made whole?' The man answers, 'I have no man', and Christ heals him with a word.
days.q: Christ asked, 'Wilt thou be made whole?' Is there anything in you that does not yet want to be healed?

days.intro: After feeding the five thousand Christ says, 'I am the bread of life.' Many go back at His words about His Flesh and Blood, and Peter answers, 'Lord, to whom shall we go? thou hast the words of eternal life.'
days.q: How do you prepare to receive the Bread of Life in Holy Communion?

days.intro: At the feast of tabernacles Christ stands and cries, 'If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink', speaking of the Holy Spirit, a Gospel read at Pentecost.
days.q: What are you thirsty for, beneath your other wants?

days.intro: Christ does not condemn a woman brought to Him in sin, and tells her to sin no more. He says, 'I am the light of the world', and 'Before Abraham was, I am.'
days.q: Christ said, 'Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.' What would you like to leave behind?

days.intro: Christ heals a man blind from his birth with clay and the pool of Siloam. Questioned again and again, the man holds to what he knows: 'whereas I was blind, now I see.'
days.q: 'Whereas I was blind, now I see.' What has Christ helped you see that you could not see before?

days.intro: Christ is the door of the sheep and the good shepherd who gives His life for the sheep. 'My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.'
days.q: How do you recognise the Shepherd's voice among the many voices around you?

days.intro: Lazarus has lain in the grave four days. Jesus weeps, then calls him out: 'Lazarus, come forth.' The Church keeps this on Lazarus Saturday, the day before Palm Sunday.
days.q: Christ said to Martha, 'I am the resurrection, and the life. Believest thou this?' How would you answer?

days.intro: Mary anoints Christ's feet, and the next day He enters Jerusalem. When Greeks ask to see Him, He speaks of the corn of wheat that must fall into the ground and die to bring forth much fruit.
days.q: The corn of wheat must die to bear fruit. What in you might need to die so that something better can grow?

days.intro: At the Supper Christ washes His disciples' feet and says, 'I have given you an example.' Then the new commandment: 'That ye love one another; as I have loved you.'
days.q: Christ washed His disciples' feet. Whose feet could you wash this week, in a practical way?

days.intro: 'Let not your heart be troubled.' Christ says He is the way, the truth, and the life, and promises the Comforter, the Holy Ghost, and a peace the world cannot give.
days.q: Christ said, 'my peace I give unto you.' What is troubling your heart that you would give to Him?

days.intro: 'I am the vine, ye are the branches.' Christ calls His disciples friends and speaks of the Spirit of truth, 'which proceedeth from the Father'.
days.q: 'Without me ye can do nothing.' Where have you been trying to do things without Him?

days.intro: Christ tells His disciples that their sorrow shall be turned into joy, and ends, 'In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.'
days.q: Which sorrow of yours would you ask Christ to turn into joy?

days.intro: Christ prays to the Father for His disciples and for all who will believe through their word: 'That they all may be one.' Read it as His prayer for you.
days.q: Christ prayed that His followers may be one. Where could you help to heal a division?

days.intro: In the garden Christ gives Himself up: 'I am he.' Before Pilate He says, 'My kingdom is not of this world', and Pilate asks, 'What is truth?'
days.q: Pilate asked 'What is truth?' with Truth Himself before him. Where do you look for truth?

days.intro: From the Cross Christ gives His Mother to the disciple: 'Behold thy mother!' He says, 'It is finished', and gives up the ghost. Blood and water come out of His side.
days.q: Christ gave His Mother to the disciple. What place does the Mother of God have in your prayer?

days.intro: Mary Magdalene weeps at the sepulchre until the risen Lord calls her by name. Eight days later Thomas confesses, 'My Lord and my God', the Gospel of Thomas Sunday.
days.q: Christ said, 'blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.' What helps your faith when you cannot see?

days.intro: By the sea of Tiberias the risen Christ makes breakfast for His disciples. Three times He asks Peter, 'lovest thou me?', and three times gives him His sheep to feed. Then: 'Follow me.'
days.q: Christ asked Peter, 'lovest thou me?' How would you answer Him, and what would He ask you to do?

pool: Which proverb from today would you like to remember this week?
Where did today's chapter describe you, for better or worse?
What does today's chapter say about the way you speak?
Which saying today would you like to pray about?
Whom did today's chapter bring to mind?
What does today's chapter teach about the poor?
Where could today's wisdom change one decision you face?
What did today's chapter say about humility?

days.intro: Solomon sets out why the book was written: to know wisdom and instruction. Its foundation comes early: 'The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.' Then Wisdom herself cries aloud in the streets.
days.q: What does 'the fear of the Lord' mean to you, beyond being afraid?

days.intro: A father urges his son to seek wisdom as silver and search for it as for treasure, for 'the Lord gives wisdom; and from his presence come knowledge and understanding.'
days.q: Where do you go looking for wisdom first, and where might you look instead?

days.intro: 'Trust in God with all thine heart; and be not exalted in thine own wisdom.' Watch for the line the Apostles James and Peter both quote: 'The Lord resists the proud; but he gives grace to the humble.'
days.q: Where are you leaning on your own understanding instead of trusting God?

days.intro: A father hands on what his own father taught him. 'Keep thine heart with the utmost care; for out of these are the issues of life.' The way of the righteous shines brighter and brighter.
days.q: What are you letting into your heart that you should guard it from?

days.intro: A warning against the adulteress and the sweetness that ends in bitterness, and a call to faithfulness in marriage: 'rejoice with the wife of thy youth.'
days.q: What small faithfulness keeps a promise strong over many years?

days.intro: 'Go to the ant, O sluggard', and in this text to the bee as well. Then the things God hates, among them a haughty eye, a lying tongue, and one who sows quarrels between brethren.
days.q: Which of the things God hates in this chapter do you most need to watch for in yourself?

days.intro: A young man without understanding follows a seductress to her house 'as an ox is led to the slaughter'. The father pleads: keep my commandments, and write them on the table of thine heart.
days.q: What helps you notice temptation early, before you are already on its road?

days.intro: Wisdom speaks in her own voice: 'I love those that love me; and they that seek me shall find me.' The Church has long heard in her Christ, whom St Paul calls the Wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:24).
days.q: Wisdom promises that those who seek her will find her. How are you seeking wisdom right now?

days.intro: 'Wisdom has built a house for herself, and set up seven pillars.' She sets her table and calls the simple to her feast, a passage read at Vespers on the feasts of the Mother of God.
days.q: Wisdom invites the simple to her table. Where do you need to come as one who still has much to learn?

days.intro: The proverbs of Solomon begin: short sayings, two lines each, setting the wise beside the foolish. Watch the many about the tongue: 'By a multitude of words thou shalt not escape sin.'
days.q: 'If thou refrain thy lips thou wilt be prudent.' Where would fewer words have helped you this week?

days.intro: Honest weights, humility, generosity: 'Wherever pride enters, there will be also disgrace.' Watch how often the generous are said to be the ones who prosper.
days.q: Where has pride brought you disgrace, and humility brought you peace?

days.intro: Sayings on instruction, work and speech: 'Some wound as they speak, like swords; but the tongues of the wise heal.'
days.q: Whose words have healed you? How could your words heal someone this week?

days.intro: 'He that keeps his own mouth keeps his own life.' Sayings on the company we keep: 'If thou walkest with wise men thou shalt be wise.'
days.q: Who are the wise people you walk with? Whom could you seek out more?

days.intro: 'There is a way which seems to be right with men, but the ends of it reach to the depths of hell.' Watch the sayings on the poor: 'he that honours him has pity upon the poor.'
days.q: What way seems right to you, that you have not yet brought to God?

days.intro: 'A submissive answer turns away wrath.' And: 'The eyes of the Lord behold both the evil and the good in every place.'
days.q: When were you last tempted to answer anger with anger? What would a gentle answer have been?

days.intro: 'Pride goes before destruction, and folly before a fall.' And: 'A man slow to anger is better than a strong man; and he that governs his temper better than he that takes a city.'
days.q: What does ruling your own spirit look like for you this week?

days.intro: 'As silver and gold are tried in a furnace, so are choice hearts with the Lord.' Sayings on peace at home and on true friendship: 'Have thou a friend for every time.'
days.q: What trial in your life might God be using to refine you?

days.intro: 'The name of the Lord is of great strength; and the righteous running to it are exalted.' And: 'Life and death are in the power of the tongue.'
days.q: When you are afraid, how do you run to the name of the Lord?

days.intro: 'He that has pity on the poor lends to the Lord.' And: 'There are many thoughts in a man's heart; but the counsel of the Lord abides for ever.'
days.q: What plan of yours would you like to place under the counsel of the Lord?

days.intro: 'Who will boast that he has a pure heart?' Sayings against revenge: 'Say not, I will avenge myself on my enemy; but wait on the Lord.'
days.q: Is there anyone you are waiting to get even with? What would waiting on the Lord look like instead?

days.intro: 'Every man seems to himself righteous; but the Lord directs the hearts.' And: 'To do justly and to speak truth, are more pleasing to God than the blood of sacrifices.'
days.q: Where might you be righteous in your own eyes but not yet in God's?

days.intro: 'A fair name is better than much wealth.' 'The rich and the poor meet together; but the Lord made them both.' Then the sayings of the wise begin.
days.q: What kind of name are you making for yourself among the people who know you?

days.intro: Sayings on appetite, riches that fly away 'like an eagle', and the heart: 'My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.'
days.q: What would it mean to give God your whole heart today?

days.intro: 'A house is built by wisdom.' And a hard saying for the heart: 'If thine enemy should fall, rejoice not over him.'
days.q: Has the fall of someone who wronged you ever pleased you? How could you pray for them instead?

days.intro: More proverbs of Solomon, copied out by the friends of King Hezekiah. 'If thine enemy hunger, feed him', the verse St Paul takes up in Romans 12.
days.q: Who is your 'enemy' this week? What could you do to feed him?

days.intro: Sayings on the fool, the sluggard and the gossip: 'With much wood fire increases; but where there is not a double-minded man, strife ceases.'
days.q: What strife in your life would go out if you stopped adding wood to it?

days.intro: 'Boast not of to-morrow; for thou knowest not what the next day shall bring forth.' And: 'Iron sharpens iron', as a friend sharpens a friend.
days.q: Who sharpens you? Whom do you sharpen?

days.intro: 'The righteous is confident as a lion.' A saying on confession: 'He that covers his own ungodliness shall not prosper: but he that blames himself shall be loved.'
days.q: What have you been covering that you would rather bring to confession?

days.intro: 'Pride brings a man low, but the Lord upholds the humble-minded with honour.' And: 'he that trusts in the Lord shall rejoice.'
days.q: Where have you seen God honour humility, in your life or someone else's?

days.intro: The words of a man who calls himself 'the most simple of all men'. His prayer asks for neither poverty nor riches: 'appoint me what is needful and sufficient.'
days.q: What would 'needful and sufficient' look like in your life right now?

days.intro: A king's mother teaches him to open his mouth for the poor and weak, and the book ends with the virtuous woman: 'Who shall find a virtuous woman? for such a one is more valuable than precious stones.'
days.q: Whose quiet strength and wisdom have shaped you? How could you thank them?
